summary: Our project uses NASA data to help farmers plan their crops more effectively. It analyzes soil conditions, weather patterns, and selected crops, then provides an adapted planting schedule. The goal is to prevent avoidable mistakes, reduce agricultural losses, and improve crop yields through better-informed decisions, helping farmers prepare for each growing season.
details:
Our project aims to make agricultural knowledge and reliable data more accessible, particularly in developing countries such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

In many communities, starting or managing an agricultural farm or business requires specialized knowledge and access to reliable agricultural data, often obtained through experienced professionals at a high cost. Our application addresses this challenge by putting essential information and practical guidance directly into users' hands.

Using NASA satellite data and environmental information, the platform uses data from soil analyzes, weather patterns, and crop requirements to provide recommendations on suitable crops, planting periods, and agricultural practices.

What makes our project innovative is the combination of accessible scientific data, practical agricultural guidance, and an integrated AI assistant. Users can independently access essential information and seek additional assistance from an expert or the application's AI assistant when facing difficulties. Our goal is not to replace experts, but to make their knowledge more accessible.

Ultimately, we aim to reduce information barriers, improve agricultural productivity, support sustainable farming, and contribute to food security.

Technology and Development

Our team used NASA datasets, HTML, JavaScript, and CSS to build the website interface, while Vercel was used for deployment and hosting.

Project name: MAKE AGRICULTURE GREAT AGAIN
